title: North American Breeding Bird Survey, BCR 15, Sierra Nevada: stop counts of 217 bird taxa on 34 routes, 2009-2025
creator: Ziolkowski, David J., Jr.; Lutmerding, Michael; Skalos, Shannon M. (U.S. Geological Survey, Eastern Ecological Science Center); English, Willow B.; Hudson, Marie-Anne R. (Environment and Climate Change Canada, Canadian Wildlife Service)
citation: Ziolkowski, D.J., Lutmerding, M., Skalos, S.M., English, W.B., and Hudson, M-A.R., 2026, North American Breeding Bird Survey Dataset 1966 - 2025: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P144YU3S. All work using these data should acknowledge the thousands of dedicated U.S. and Canadian participants who annually perform and coordinate the survey.

abstract: The standard runs (RPID 101) of the 50-stop routes of Bird Conservation Region 15 (Sierra Nevada; California), 2009-2025, one row per run, stop and bird taxon: y is the count at that stop (breeding-category plus non-breeder records), zero for each of the 217 taxa recorded in these runs and not seen at the stop. Stops after the last stop with evidence of sampling have no row. Vehicle and noise records per stop come with it. Stops are sequential points about 800 m apart, counted once in one morning, not temporal repeats.
samplingProtocol: North American Breeding Bird Survey: a 3-minute point count of all birds seen within 400 m or heard at each of up to 50 stops per route; the stop-level record exists for every run from 1997, here from 2009.
closureNote: period = year (index year - 1965); occasion = stop number along the route (1 to the last stop with evidence). Stops are sequential spatial points about 800 m apart along a route of about 39.2 km, counted once, in one morning of about five hours, by one moving observer: they are not temporal repeats at one place, so no closure of the kind that N-mixture or occupancy models assume holds across stops. A bird can be counted at two stops. On spatial subunits as replicates see Kendall and White (2009, doi:10.1111/j.1365-2664.2009.01732.x); on N-mixture reliability, Barker et al. (2018, doi:10.1111/biom.12734) and Link et al. (2018, doi:10.1002/ecy.2362). Across years a route's rows are not a closed population.
surveyEvidenceNote: Weather.csv lists every run but no file says how many stops a run sampled. Evidence that a stop was sampled: a bird record in 50-StopData or Migrants, or Car > 0 or Noise > 0 in VehicleData. K = the last stop with evidence; stops 1 to K are surveys, and a zero at an empty stop before K is fair because the observer went on past it. Stops after K have no row and their number is in notShipped. A mid-route skip inside a run cannot be seen in this deposit, so a stop zero there could be unsupported; nationally obs_quality_current = 0 marks more than 85% of runs from 1997 with K below 45. Pool: every taxon recorded in this table's runs, in the breeding or the non-breeder stop files.
geographicCoverage: Bird Conservation Region 15 (Sierra Nevada; BCR code and name as in this release's Routes.csv and metadata), roadside routes in California; route start points as published

coordinatesCoarsened.method: route start points as USGS publishes them; agency coordinates are kept as published under E7

covariateNote: obs_nonbreeder_count: the recorded non-breeder count at the stop, 0 where none. obs_cars: the vehicle count at the stop where RecordedCar = 1 (the metadata: recorded at all sampled stops) or Car > 0, else NA, because the metadata makes no promise for a 0 there. obs_noise: 1 if excessive noise from sources other than passing vehicles (more than 45 seconds, interfering with hearing birds) was recorded at the stop, 0 if not, NA where the run has no VehicleData row. Codes, from the release metadata: wind is Beaufort 0 to 8; sky is 0 clear or few clouds, 1 partly cloudy or variable, 2 cloudy or overcast, 4 fog or smoke, 5 drizzle, 7 snow, 8 showers; obs_assistant is 1 if an assistant recorded the data; obs_quality_current is 1 if the run met all quality criteria (manual inspection before 1997, by rule from 1997); minutes are after midnight; wind or sky code 9 (no data) is NA.
designNote: One row per run, stop and taxon; occasion = stop. Stops past the last stop with evidence of sampling have no row.

notShipped.runs_outside_the_design: 728 of the 1095 runs in BCR 15 are outside this table: 728 before 2009 and 0 from 2009 that are not RPID 101 on a Detail 1 or 2 route; they are in the national count table
notShipped.stops_after_last_stop_with_evidence: 111 stops of this table's runs, past K
notShipped.stop_rows_before_2009: stop-level rows of BCR 15 before 2009 are in the deposit and not shipped, for size; the block table covers all years
notShipped.TotalSpp: per-run count of breeding records; an assertion; not shipped
notShipped.StopTotal: per-taxon number of stops with the taxon; derivable from y; not shipped

notes: BCR codes and names are this release's (1 to 37); bbsBayes2 has since renumbered some. USGS and bbsBayes2 analyse RunType 1 only: filter obs_run_type == 1. RPID 501/502 (experimental) lower counts on average (Sauer et al. 2019, doi:10.1093/condor/duz009). y - obs_nonbreeder_count is the published breeding count. taxon_first_year and taxon_last_year in __taxa are national; a zero before taxon_first_year can mean the category did not exist yet. Unidentified groups, forms and hybrids are their own taxa, with nothing rolled up. Route covariates and route start points (not bird locations) are in __units, so eco_to_unmarked() starts with empty siteCovs; join on unit. Temperatures are as recorded, value plus scale; impossible values are kept. period = year - 1965 in every table, with the calendar year in __periods, which lists every year from the table's first to its last; a year without a run has n_runs = 0. 2020 had no field work (no row in any data file), so period 55 never occurs. eco_to_unmarked(family = "colext") builds numPrimary = max(period) and one column per (period, occasion) present, so a year without a run breaks it or misaligns it: filter to occasion == 1 and pad the periods yourself before fitting a dynamic occupancy model. Stop table: runs from 2009 on, so non-breeder records are preserved throughout (obs_nonbreeder_count is 0 where none) and stop data are complete. Rationale: notes/decisions/bbs_design.md.
